title: CLAUDE.md
text: R/patterns.R owns central pattern registry — named list pattern functions stored package environment (.pattern_registry, emptyenv()-parented env). pattern function signature: x/y/width/height npc units (0–1 relative parent viewport), gp base gpar() geom (carries pattern_colour, pattern_linewidth), params named list extra parameters scale (pattern_angle, pattern_spacing, pattern_size). Patterns render content inside clipped viewport via clipped_grob() helper (clips bbox rectangle). hatch_lines() shared helper line-based patterns (hatch, crosshatch, horizontal, vertical) computes line positions via perpendicular-offset arithmetic across unit square; poly_x/poly_y supplied calls clip_segments_to_poly() restrict lines polygon interior. pip() vectorised ray-casting point--polygon test used dots. Custom patterns registered runtime register_pattern(name, fn). Built-patterns: none, hatch, crosshatch, horizontal, vertical, dots, weave. , hatch crosshatch currently honor pattern_angle — others fixed orientations design (oversight; see ROADMAP).
code: fn(x, y, width, height, gp, params) → grid grob

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Five geoms extend existing ggplot2 ggproto classes: GeomColPattern / GeomBarPattern (R/geom_col_pattern.R) — extend GeomRect (GeomBar). deliberate: ggplot2 4.0 restructured GeomBar longer expose draw_panel method can safely override. GeomRect draws filled rectangles xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax, bars become stat + position stack runs. setup_data() derives xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax x/y bar case. GeomPolygonPattern (R/geom_polygon_pattern.R) — extends GeomPolygon; clips pattern exact polygon shape using device-independent -R computation. Polygon vertices normalised 0–1 bbox-relative coordinates passed pattern functions params$poly_x / params$poly_y. Line patterns use clip_segments_to_poly() (parametric intersection + ray-casting midpoint test, supports concave simple polygons); dots uses pip() directly filter grid positions. GeomRibbonPattern / GeomAreaPattern (R/geom_ribbon_pattern.R) — extend GeomRibbon via draw_group override. base ribbon rendered parent; pattern overlay reconstructs ribbon polygon (upper ymax edge + reversed lower ymin edge) coord$transform output feeds existing clip_segments_to_poly / pip clipper. GeomAreaPattern thin subclass sets ymin = 0, ymax = y setup_data, mirroring GeomArea. orientation = "y" supported pattern overlay. GeomViolinPattern (R/geom_violin_pattern.R) — extends GeomViolin via draw_group override. Reconstructs violin polygon xminv/xmaxv arithmetic GeomViolin uses internally, transforms npc, clips pattern violin outline. Requires violinwidth column (computed stat_ydensity); emits message returns nullGrob() absent. orientation = "y" supported pattern overlay. draw_panel() / draw_group() renders geometric primitive base grob plus clipped pattern grob stacked grobTree. draw_key_pattern() function R/aaa_draw_key.R (prefixed aaa_ loads first alphabetically — geoms reference definition time) renders legend swatches. Legend swatches use 2.5× spacing multiplier patterns don’t appear dense blob small key area.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: R/scale_pattern.R provides three discrete scales map variable pattern names: scale_pattern_manual() — explicit name→pattern mapping scale_pattern_discrete() — cycles built-patterns automatically scale_pattern_identity() — uses column value directly pattern name

title: CLAUDE.md
text: pattern_angle intentionally ignored horizontal, vertical, dots, weave — names composite structure define fixed orientation. hatch crosshatch rotate. Legend key spacing uses hardcoded 2.5× multiplier pattern_spacing. Per-row pattern parameter mapping (e.g. mapping pattern_spacing column) untested. Performance O(n) grobs — can slow large datasets.

title: Getting Started with ggpatchy
text: geom_col_pattern() geom_bar_pattern() drop-replacements geom_col() geom_bar(). Map pattern discrete variable scale_pattern_manual() scale_pattern_discrete().  geom_bar_pattern() uses stat = "count":
code: df <- data.frame(   category = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),   value    = c(3.2, 5.1, 4.0, 2.7) )  ggplot(df, aes(category, value, fill = category, pattern = category)) +   geom_col_pattern() +   scale_pattern_manual(values = c(     A = "hatch", B = "crosshatch", C = "dots", D = "vertical"   )) +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "geom_col_pattern()") ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill = class, pattern = class)) +   geom_bar_pattern() +   scale_pattern_discrete() +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)) +   labs(title = "geom_bar_pattern() with scale_pattern_discrete()")

title: Getting Started with ggpatchy
text: geom_polygon_pattern() clips patterns exact polygon boundary, just bounding box. means concave shapes like crescents L-shapes handled correctly.
code: theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 7)[-7] hex <- data.frame(x = cos(theta), y = sin(theta))  ggplot(hex, aes(x, y)) +   geom_polygon_pattern(     pattern        = "hatch",     fill           = "lightyellow",     pattern_colour = "goldenrod",     pattern_angle  = 30,     pattern_spacing = 0.07   ) +   coord_fixed() +   theme_void() +   labs(title = "geom_polygon_pattern() on a hexagon")

title: Getting Started with ggpatchy
text: geom_ribbon_pattern() adds patterns confidence bands region defined ymin ymax.  Multiple groups different patterns:
code: x  <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 80) df <- data.frame(x = x, ymin = sin(x) - 0.3, ymax = sin(x) + 0.3)  ggplot(df, aes(x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax)) +   geom_ribbon_pattern(     pattern        = "hatch",     fill           = "lightblue",     pattern_colour = "steelblue"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "geom_ribbon_pattern() — confidence band") df2 <- data.frame(   x       = c(x, x),   ymin    = c(sin(x) - 0.2, cos(x) + 0.5),   ymax    = c(sin(x) + 0.2, cos(x) + 1.0),   group   = rep(c("sin", "cos"), each = length(x)),   pattern = rep(c("hatch", "crosshatch"), each = length(x)),   fill    = rep(c("lightblue", "lightyellow"), each = length(x)) )  ggplot(df2, aes(x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,                 group = group, fill = fill, pattern = pattern)) +   geom_ribbon_pattern(alpha = 0.8) +   scale_pattern_identity(guide = "legend") +   scale_fill_identity() +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "geom_ribbon_pattern() — two groups")

title: Getting Started with ggpatchy

title: Getting Started with ggpatchy
text: stat = "identity" geom_violin_pattern() requires violinwidth column. default stat ("ydensity") computes violinwidth automatically raw data. pass stat = "identity" pre-summarised density data, data frame must include violinwidth column (values [0, 1] giving normalised half-width y level). column absent, geom_violin_pattern() emits informative message skips group rather crashing. orientation = "y" (horizontal) supported pattern overlays. geom_violin_pattern(), geom_ribbon_pattern(), geom_area_pattern() skip pattern orientation = "y" flipped_aes = TRUE. base shape still renders correctly. Use coord_flip() vertical geom workaround. Polygon clipping bounding-box relative: Pattern spacing coordinates computed relative polygon’s bounding box, panel viewport. thin elongated shapes (e.g. narrow violins, skinny ribbon bands) may show denser sparser patterns wide shapes pattern_spacing value. Non-Cartesian coordinates: Patterns drawn screen (npc) space coord$transform(). coord_polar coord_sf pattern lines remain straight screen pixels rather following coordinate curvature.

title: Mapping with Patterns
text: North Carolina county dataset bundled sf package lets us encode two census variables simultaneously: county area (AREA, continuous) mapped fill colour, 1974 birth-rate tertile (BIR74, cut three equal-count bins) mapped pattern. Readers can see dimensions — pattern distinguishes high-birth-rate counties regardless whether also happen large small.
code: library(ggplot2) library(sf) #> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE library(ggpatchy)  nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)  # Quantile-based tertiles give balanced bin sizes across skewed BIR74 data nc$birth_bin <- cut(   nc$BIR74,   breaks        = quantile(nc$BIR74, probs = c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1)),   include.lowest = TRUE,   labels        = c("Low", "Medium", "High") )  ggplot(nc) +   geom_sf_pattern(     aes(fill = AREA, pattern = birth_bin),     pattern_colour    = "grey30",     pattern_linewidth = 0.4,     pattern_spacing   = 0.12   ) +   scale_pattern_manual(     values = c(Low = "hatch", Medium = "crosshatch", High = "dots"),     name   = "Birth rate (1974)"   ) +   scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Oranges", name = "Area") +   labs(     title    = "North Carolina counties",     subtitle = "Fill: county area  ·  Pattern: 1974 birth-rate tertile"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(axis.text = element_blank())

title: Mapping with Patterns
text: spData package’s us_states dataset maps 2015 population (total_pop_15) fill colour US Census region pattern. Four patterns — one per region — distinguish Midwest, Northeast, South, West without adding second colour scale. combination lets readers ask two questions : populous state? (colour) region ? (pattern). questions answerable black--white printout.
code: library(spData) #> To access larger datasets in this package, install the spDataLarge #> package with: `install.packages('spDataLarge', #> repos='https://nowosad.github.io/drat/', type='source')`  # Fix a known typo in the REGION factor level us <- us_states levels(us$REGION)[levels(us$REGION) == "Norteast"] <- "Northeast"  ggplot(us) +   geom_sf_pattern(     aes(fill = total_pop_15, pattern = REGION),     pattern_colour    = "grey20",     pattern_linewidth = 0.45,     pattern_spacing   = 0.09   ) +   scale_pattern_manual(     values = c(       Midwest   = "hatch",       Northeast = "crosshatch",       South     = "dots",       West      = "vertical"     ),     name = "Region"   ) +   scale_fill_distiller(     palette   = "Blues",     direction = 1,     name      = "Population (2015)",     labels    = scales::comma   ) +   labs(     title    = "US states",     subtitle = "Fill: 2015 population  ·  Pattern: Census region"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Pattern Fill Overlays for ggplot2 Geoms
text: Register function takes bounding box shape (npc) plus graphical parameters, returns grid grob: registering, use like built-pattern:
code: library(grid)  register_pattern("zigzag", function(x, y, width, height, gp, params) {   spacing <- params$pattern_spacing %||% 0.1   line_gp <- gpar(col = gp$pattern_colour %||% "black",                   lwd = gp$pattern_linewidth %||% 1)   ys <- seq(0, 1, by = spacing)   segs <- lapply(ys, function(y0) {     polylineGrob(       x  = unit(c(0, 0.5, 1), "npc"),       y  = unit(c(y0, y0 + spacing / 2, y0), "npc"),       gp = line_gp     )   })   vp <- viewport(x = x, y = y, width = width, height = height,                  just = c("left", "bottom"), clip = "on")   gTree(children = do.call(gList, segs), vp = vp) }) ggplot(df, aes(group, value, fill = group, pattern = group)) +   geom_col_pattern() +   scale_pattern_manual(values = c(A = "zigzag", B = "hatch", C = "dots"))
